_doc: Addon recipes that collide in GTM 7.5.3's recipe lookup and lose a route or run the wrong recipe. GTM keeps one recipe per ingredient path (AGENTS.md, 'One recipe per lookup path'): of two recipes of one type on one path, or one whose path runs into the other's, only one ever runs, though EMI shows both. Found by the bench guard tools/test/overlay/kubejs/server_scripts/gg_test_recipe_lookup.js (runs lookup-guard-1 and -2, 2026-10-25); the guard asks GTM's lookup for every recipe below after this table is applied.
remove   the recipes in `ids` go away. `keeps` is the correct recipe on the same path: if it is missing nothing is removed (an error is logged), so the route never disappears.

circuit  each recipe in `ids` is read back as JSON, removed and added again with GTM's KubeJS builder under grindless:<type>/<old path>: the same inputs in the same order, chances, EU, duration, data and conditions, with its programmed circuit set to `circuit` (added after the items when it had none). GTM's .circuit(n) on an existing recipe ADDS a second circuit, and a recipe with two circuits never runs: that is why the recipe is rebuilt, not edited.
Same-result duplicates (GTM's generated recipe and an addon's copy, GCYR's twin recipe, GT--'s raw palladium _large variant) are not here: they stay in the guard's baseline.

collisions.reason: GT-- registers its LV pentlandite sulfuric attack three times on one path: tiny_dust1 is an exact copy of dust1_lv and tiny_dust2 its typo (pentlandite in, sulfuric copper solution out; chalcopyrite has dust2_lv). The typo was the one that ran in the chemical reactor.
The same three recipes in the large chemical reactor: only dust1_lv stays.

GT-- (anthracene) and GCYR (durene) both rewrite GTM's coal tar distillation, and both distillery copies take circuit 5: only durene ran, and anthracene, made nowhere else, never did (GT--'s chemical plant hydrogen peroxide needs it). Circuits 1-5 are coal tar's other cuts; 6 is free.

GT--'s Supplementaries bomb is GTM's dynamite (paper, string, glyceryl trinitrate) plus circuit 1, so one path runs into the other: the bomb never ran in the chemical reactor and dynamite never in the large one. Dynamite takes circuit 2, free for those inputs.

GTCA's trinium naquadah carbonite and GCYR's trinaquadalloy are both trinium, naquadah and carbon dust on circuit 3: only trinaquadalloy ran. Circuit 6 is free for those dusts (2 is trinium naquadah's, 13 the gas variants').
